alex (sales): Hey team — VerityBank POC hitting ~3.5s TTFT for short prompts even with prefill on. Customer link: https://console.veritabank.example/poc. Anyone available to triage?

maria (solutions): On it. @jamie can you pull traces and node metrics? What model/variant are they on?

verity-eng: We're on `redwood/open-rt-7b-q4` pinned v1.2. Prefill = true, batch_window_ms = 20, continuous_batching = false. Seeing consistent 3.5s, occasional spikes to ~6s. No 429s.

jamie (oncall): grabbing logs now. RequestID=rb-99321 shows long first-token. Snippet:
```
[2024-04-14T12:10:23Z] request=rb-99321 enter_queue latency=2.1ms batch_wait=21ms kvcache_miss=true model_open=25ms first_token_ms=3520
[2024-04-14T12:10:23Z] cpu_steal=28% host=host-07 gpu_util=62% batcher_queue=12
```

maria (solutions): kvcache_miss=true — looks like prefix/KV cache isn't hitting. Are they sending unique conversation ids per request? That can bork cache shard locality. @sre-bot plz check node-side GC / batcher spikes.

sre-bot: Observed batcher_queue_depth spike on gpu-8b-07 @2024-04-14T12:10; background GC on host-07; cpu_steal elevated; ephemeral disk IO high. No 429s returned.

alex (sales): Customer confirms they supply a unique `conversation_id` per request (one-per-message). Could explain cache misses — keys aren't reusable.

maria (solutions): Exactly. If conversation_id is fully unique per message, prefix KV can't be reused. Suggest canonicalizing cache keys: hash(truncate(prompt_prefix)) or use a stable convo id for warmup batches. Suggest config change: `cache_key = conversation_id || prompt_hash(truncate=256)` to allow reuse.

verity-eng: If we change cache key policy, any billing or security implications? We need a short answer for our procurement team.

alex (sales): Short answer on billing: prefill warms tokens so token count up a bit (~+3-8% depending on prompt), but total compute per apparent request drops because KV recompute avoided. I'll draft quick numbers. Security: no plaintext persisted, cache respects tenancy; we'll provide doc.

jamie (oncall): Quick workaround you can try immediately: lower `batch_window_ms` and enable continuous batching so short requests aggregate faster. Example config we used for a canary:
```
prefill: true
batch_window_ms: 8
continuous_batching: true
cache_key_mode: predictive
```
This reduced queue_wait and made more requests join the same batch.

maria (solutions): Also check that the client isn't sending a unique timestamp or nonce inside the cache-key-affecting prefix. If so, strip the nonce on the server side for cache purposes.

verity-eng: We spun a canary with the config above for 15 minutes. Results: median TTFT = 220ms, p95 = 420ms. Big improvement. No increase in 429s.

alex (sales): Great. I'll send the pricing delta: rough estimate +5% token usage on prefill for this workload, but TTFT wins usually improve UX and reduce overall compute billing. Will follow up in thread with numbers. :thumbsup:

maria (solutions): I'll prepare a short rollout guide (canary → canary-sized steady state → scale) and include the cache-key snippet and a note about broadcast warmups. Also flag VPC egress + SOC2 items for the security questionnaire.

jamie (oncall): I'll keep monitoring gpu-8b-07 overnight and watch for GC spikes. If anything reappears, ping me directly.

verity-eng: Thanks everyone — we'll proceed with the recommended config change and wait for your pricing doc. Initial testing looks promising.

maria (solutions): Awesome. Marking this POC triage as done for now, will follow up with rollout doc and pricing. :rocket:

jamie (oncall): resolved unless new anomalies show up — keeping a watch.

alex (sales): Thanks team. I'll loop in procurement with the short answers and attach SOC2 + VPC notes.
